description: WHO, UNESCO, UNICEF, FAO, ILO — HQ + mandate

questions.stem: The World Health Organization (WHO) is headquartered at:
questions.explanation: WHO — Geneva. Founded 7 April 1948 (now World Health Day). Specialised UN agency for public health. 194 member states. Current DG (2025): Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus (Ethiopia). Led global response to H1N1, Ebola, COVID-19.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.explanation: UNESCO — United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization. HQ: Paris (founded 1945). Programs: World Heritage Sites, literacy, free press, teaching of climate change, MGIEP (Gandhi Institute for Education for Peace, Delhi). UNHCR — refugees. ILO — labour. UNICEF — children. incl. World Heritage Sites.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

_fixes.was: Education, science, culture (incl. World Heritage Sites)

questions.stem: Match the UN AGENCY with its HQ. A. FAO.  B. ILO.  C. IAEA.  D. IMO. List-II: 1. Rome.  2. Geneva.  3. Vienna.  4. London.
questions.explanation: FAO (Food & Agriculture Org) — Rome. ILO (International Labour Org) — Geneva. IAEA (International Atomic Energy Agency) — Vienna. IMO (International Maritime Org) — London.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The HEADQUARTERS of the UNITED NATIONS is in:
questions.explanation: UN HQ — 17-acre site in Manhattan, New York. Internationally-governed zone (not US territory). 4 other UN offices: Geneva, Vienna, Nairobi, and since 2019, Rome. Secretary-General (2025): António Guterres (Portugal, 2nd term). Turtle Bay, Manhattan.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The ILO (International Labour Organization) was founded in:
questions.explanation: ILO — 1919, one of the oldest UN bodies, founded as part of the League of Nations after WWI (Treaty of Versailles). Became a specialised UN agency in 1946. HQ: Geneva. Unique 'tripartite' structure — governments + employers + workers represented. after WWI, Treaty of Versailles.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

options.option_text: Children's welfare + humanitarian aid to children worldwide

questions.explanation: UNICEF — United Nations Children's Fund. HQ: New York. Founded 1946 (originally 'UN International Children's Emergency Fund'). Nobel Peace Prize 1965. Key campaigns: polio eradication, immunisation, nutrition, girl-child education, WASH (water-sanitation-hygiene).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The 'WORLD INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY ORGANIZATION' (WIPO) is headquartered at:
questions.explanation: WIPO — Geneva. Set up 1967, became UN agency 1974. Handles patents, copyrights, trademarks, design rights, geographical indications. India joined WIPO in 1975. Famous annual 'Global Innovation Index' (GII).
